world.title: Iraqi police advance toward militia stronghold after reported deal
world.summary: Iraqi Federal Police moved toward the entrance to Jurf al-Sakhar on Friday, beginning a staged security operation after Baghdad and the Iran-backed Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah reportedly reached a compromise to avoid a direct clash. The advance followed a two-hour delay; reports had not confirmed whether forces ente
world.content: Iraqi Federal Police moved toward the entrance to Jurf al-Sakhar on Friday, beginning a staged security operation after Baghdad and the Iran-backed Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah reportedly reached a compromise to avoid a direct clash. The advance followed a two-hour delay; reports had not confirmed whether forces entered the area or took over militia-held positions. Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered the deployment after a government investigation accused Kataib Hezbollah of siphoning hundreds of millions of dollars in state oil since 2021; the group denies the allegation. A new joint command is intended to coordinate security forces and protect oil sites, but how the militia will relinquish or share control remains unsettled. Iraq has set June 30, 2027, as the deadline for armed groups to bring their weapons under state control.
world.image_alt: Iraqi police advance toward militia stronghold after reported deal

world.title: Hasina supporters’ shutdown sparks arson and deadly violence in Bangladesh
world.summary: Arson attacks, transport disruption and deadly clashes hit Bangladesh on Nov. 19 as supporters of the banned Awami League held a nationwide shutdown ahead of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s planned return from India in December. The party called the shutdown after the government rejected her request for new trave
world.content: Arson attacks, transport disruption and deadly clashes hit Bangladesh on Nov. 19 as supporters of the banned Awami League held a nationwide shutdown ahead of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s planned return from India in December. The party called the shutdown after the government rejected her request for new travel documents. Hasina faces a death sentence imposed in absentia last year. Police said two members of the governing Bangladesh Nationalist Party were killed on Wednesday night. Attackers set fire to or vandalized the ancestral homes of former interim leader Muhammad Yunus and BNP lawmakers and attacked vehicles and part of a railway line. Yunus’ family members were safe. Police also reported crude-bomb blasts and fires across multiple districts. The government deployed 97 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh across seven districts, and police said they had arrested 107 people suspected of links to the Awami League in Dhaka over 24 hours. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman accused the party of seeking to destabilize the country. Separately, garment workers demanding higher wages blocked a highway, forcing factories to close.

world.title: Russian strikes kill one in Kyiv, damage two embassies
world.summary: Russian strikes on Kyiv on Thursday, Nov. 19, killed one person, injured five and damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies, Ukrainian officials and the Austrian and Dutch foreign ministers said. Embassy staff were unharmed, but the attack also damaged residential buildings and St. Volodymyr’s Cathedral in the capital.
world.content: Russian strikes on Kyiv on Thursday, Nov. 19, killed one person, injured five and damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies, Ukrainian officials and the Austrian and Dutch foreign ministers said. Embassy staff were unharmed, but the attack also damaged residential buildings and St. Volodymyr’s Cathedral in the capital. Ukraine said Russia fired anti-ship missiles and 98 drones across the country, with strikes recorded at 18 locations. The Austrian mission reported shattered windows and damaged vehicles. A projectile landed outside during working hours, when about 10 people were inside. The Dutch mission also sustained damage, while debris fell on the grounds of Brazil’s embassy and Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry. The European Union said it would summon Russia’s representative in Brussels and increase support for Ukraine. Austria ordered additional measures to protect its embassy staff, while the Netherlands summoned the Russian ambassador to discuss the damage. No evidence has established a link between the embassy strikes and a Dutch weapons maker’s announcement that Ukraine had used its arms in an attack on the Crimean Bridge earlier that week.
world.image_alt: Russian strikes kill one in Kyiv, damage two embassies

world.title: COP31 draft drops fossil-fuel phase-out and adaptation funding target
world.summary: Australia, co-leading negotiations at the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, issued a revised COP31 draft on Nov. 19 that removed every reference to coal, oil and gas, including an earlier call to accelerate a fossil-fuel phase-out. The nine-page text was half the length of the previous version; nearly 200 count
world.content: Australia, co-leading negotiations at the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, issued a revised COP31 draft on Nov. 19 that removed every reference to coal, oil and gas, including an earlier call to accelerate a fossil-fuel phase-out. The nine-page text was half the length of the previous version; nearly 200 countries were due to reach a consensus deal by the summit’s scheduled close on Nov. 20. The revision also dropped a commitment sought by developing countries to provide at least $120 billion a year for climate adaptation by 2035. Instead, it calls for further talks on tripling adaptation finance but specifies no amount. The draft retains a proposal to raise electricity’s share of global final energy demand to 35% by 2035 but does not require the additional electricity to come from clean sources. Negotiators entered the summit’s final scheduled day still divided on the draft. Australia’s Climate Minister Chris Bowen said consultations would continue through the night; climate conferences have often run past their official deadlines.
world.image_alt: COP31 draft drops fossil-fuel phase-out and adaptation funding target

world.title: House releases China chip license records; California subpoenas Nvidia
world.summary: The U.S. House Foreign Affairs Committee on Nov. 19 released records showing the Commerce Department approved exports of 879,868 advanced artificial-intelligence chips to Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, out of 3,444,160 chips requested. The licenses covered Nvidia H200 and Advanced Micro Devices
world.content: The U.S. House Foreign Affairs Committee on Nov. 19 released records showing the Commerce Department approved exports of 879,868 advanced artificial-intelligence chips to Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026, out of 3,444,160 chips requested. The licenses covered Nvidia H200 and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) MI325X processors. Recipients included Alibaba, Tencent, Baidu and BYD. Some named companies were on the Pentagon’s list of Chinese military-linked firms, though Alibaba’s applications predated its addition to the list in June 2026. Separately, California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia for information on whether chips or confidential company information reached China and whether Nvidia misled investors. The inquiry follows the Nov. 11 departure of co-founder and former chief executive Jensen Huang after reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive whom U.S. officials suspect of ties to Chinese intelligence. The subpoena is an investigative step, not a finding of wrongdoing. Nvidia said the licenses imposed strict conditions and volume limits and that it had stopped shipping H200 chips to China. The approvals do not establish that all licensed chips were delivered. Commerce official Jeffrey Kessler told lawmakers in July that shipments had begun but were “very few.” Huang is scheduled to appear before House committees on Dec. 1, followed by Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter on Dec. 2.
world.image_alt: House releases China chip license records; California subpoenas Nvidia

world.title: UK jury convicts four men in drug-facilitated abuse case
world.summary: A jury at Winchester Crown Court convicted four men on Nov. 19 of rape and other sexual offences against Joanne Young, whose then-husband, former local councillor Philip Young, drugged her and recruited men online to sexually assault her. Two defendants were convicted of rape; the other two were convicted of sexual off
world.content: A jury at Winchester Crown Court convicted four men on Nov. 19 of rape and other sexual offences against Joanne Young, whose then-husband, former local councillor Philip Young, drugged her and recruited men online to sexually assault her. Two defendants were convicted of rape; the other two were convicted of sexual offences including assault by penetration. Philip Young had pleaded guilty to 56 offences, including 11 counts of rape and 11 of administering a substance with intent. The abuse took place at the couple’s home in Swindon between 2016 and 2023. Police uncovered it after investigating extreme images posted online and searching Philip Young’s devices. The four men argued that they believed Joanne Young had consented, but prosecutors said they had not checked with her. She waived her right to anonymity and urged the government to review how the law treats consent. The Crown Prosecution Service described the case as the first in England in which a jury convicted men of sexually assaulting a woman whose husband drugged her and organized the abuse. The four convicted men, Philip Young and a sixth man who pleaded guilty are due to be sentenced at Winchester Crown Court on Dec. 21 and 22.
world.image_alt: UK jury convicts four men in drug-facilitated abuse case

world.title: Russian strikes kill three in Kyiv, damage bridges after Crimea attack
world.summary: Russian forces struck three bridges across Kyiv’s Dnipro River with missiles overnight into Friday, killing at least three people and injuring about 15, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The attack followed Ukrainian strikes that damaged the Kerch Bridge linking Russia with occupied Crimea and further disrupted crossin
world.content: Russian forces struck three bridges across Kyiv’s Dnipro River with missiles overnight into Friday, killing at least three people and injuring about 15, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. The attack followed Ukrainian strikes that damaged the Kerch Bridge linking Russia with occupied Crimea and further disrupted crossings between the Ukrainian capital’s two banks. The Podilsko-Voskresensky crossing was closed in one direction, while the Darnytskyi and Southern bridges were hit. Traffic restrictions and emergency power outages also affected Kyiv. Russia’s Defense Ministry said it had targeted military-industrial, energy and transport infrastructure in Kyiv and other regions, without providing evidence for the claim. The wider overnight barrage also damaged a hospital in Kharkiv, where four people were wounded, and injured civilians in other cities. After the Kerch Bridge attacks, Russian President Vladimir Putin said Moscow would not pursue proposed limited ceasefires on energy infrastructure and Black Sea shipping, and threatened a more painful response. European leaders met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Berlin, while U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said President Donald Trump was open to an Article 5-like security guarantee for Ukraine.
world.image_alt: Russian strikes kill three in Kyiv, damage bridges after Crimea attack

world.title: Houthi strike damages Saudi wealth fund tower in Riyadh
world.summary: Saudi authorities said a Houthi attack damaged several floors of a tower in Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District and two nearby buildings on Thursday, Nov. 19. They reported no injuries. Witnesses and images identified the building as the Public Investment Fund (PIF) Tower, home to Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth
world.content: Saudi authorities said a Houthi attack damaged several floors of a tower in Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District and two nearby buildings on Thursday, Nov. 19. They reported no injuries. Witnesses and images identified the building as the Public Investment Fund (PIF) Tower, home to Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. The Saudi-led coalition said it had responded to a missile threat and that debris caused the damage. The Houthis later claimed they had targeted the financial district twice that day. The 80-storey, 385-metre tower houses the PIF, which manages more than $900 billion and is central to the kingdom’s economic diversification plans. The strike was the second attack in less than two weeks to damage a landmark in Riyadh’s financial district; an Aramco building was hit on Nov. 8. Fighting in Yemen, where Saudi Arabia backs the internationally recognised government against the Houthis, has continued to intensify since resuming in July. Saudi officials have told Western officials they expect the campaign to last up to six months and want their allies to make gains before negotiations with the Houthis. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met U.S. Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper in Riyadh on Thursday to discuss military ties and regional developments.
world.image_alt: Houthi strike damages Saudi wealth fund tower in Riyadh

business.title: Bitcoin falls below $62,000 as ETF withdrawals and rate fears mount
business.summary: Bitcoin briefly fell below $62,000 on Friday, touching $61,381, as a weeklong decline deepened and investors withdrew money from U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Bitcoin later traded around $63,000 in South Korea, after losing about 13% over the week; it had also recorded six consecutive weekly declines.
business.content: Bitcoin briefly fell below $62,000 on Friday, touching $61,381, as a weeklong decline deepened and investors withdrew money from U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs). Bitcoin later traded around $63,000 in South Korea, after losing about 13% over the week; it had also recorded six consecutive weekly declines. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded about $2.9 billion in withdrawals so far in November, including $306.5 million on Nov. 18. The withdrawals have coincided with a sell-off in technology shares and growing expectations of further Federal Reserve rate increases. Some analysts also suggested investors were freeing up cash for artificial-intelligence company Anthropic’s stock-market debut, though that link has not been established. Traders are watching whether Bitcoin can hold $60,000 and looking to the Federal Reserve’s next meeting for its rate decision.
business.image_alt: Bitcoin falls below $62,000 as ETF withdrawals and rate fears mount

business.title: Trump, Xi and Putin pledge to increase refined-fuel supply, with few details
business.summary: The United States, China and Russia pledged to increase production and supply of refined petroleum products in a declaration issued after President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen on Nov. 19. The declaration offered no concrete measures to carry out the pl
business.content: The United States, China and Russia pledged to increase production and supply of refined petroleum products in a declaration issued after President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen on Nov. 19. The declaration offered no concrete measures to carry out the pledge. At the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, Xi promoted China as a market opportunity to business leaders and called for fewer barriers to trade and investment. U.S. tariffs covered 60 trading partners that together account for 99.4% of U.S. imports, while U.S. restrictions on Chinese firms' access to chips remained a source of tension.

business.title: Nvidia shares 36% below record as Moody’s cuts outlook
business.summary: Moody’s Ratings lowered Nvidia’s credit outlook to stable from positive, citing uncertainty after longtime chief executive Jensen Huang left the company. It kept Nvidia’s Aa1 debt rating but said an upgrade was unlikely over the next 12 to 18 months. The move followed Nvidia’s report of $115.84 billion in third-quarter
business.content: Moody’s Ratings lowered Nvidia’s credit outlook to stable from positive, citing uncertainty after longtime chief executive Jensen Huang left the company. It kept Nvidia’s Aa1 debt rating but said an upgrade was unlikely over the next 12 to 18 months. The move followed Nvidia’s report of $115.84 billion in third-quarter revenue, more than twice the year-earlier level, and a $130 billion forecast for the current quarter. The board has ruled out Huang’s return and hired Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent chief executive. Nvidia raised its fiscal 2028 revenue-growth outlook to about 75%, while its shares remained 36% below their October record close. Moody’s also warned that investigations could distract management and that Huang’s departure may affect Nvidia’s strategy and relationships across the AI industry. Nvidia’s current forecast includes no licensed Hopper data-center chip shipments to China, after the company recorded $2.4 billion in such sales during the quarter.
business.image_alt: Nvidia shares 36% below record as Moody’s cuts outlook

business.title: California subpoenas Nvidia in investor-disclosure inquiry as shares slide
business.summary: California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia on Nov. 19, seeking records to determine whether advanced chips or confidential company information reached China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public. The inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing. Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for com
business.content: California Attorney General Rob Bonta subpoenaed Nvidia on Nov. 19, seeking records to determine whether advanced chips or confidential company information reached China and whether Nvidia misled investors and the public. The inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing. Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Shares of the Santa Clara-based chipmaker fell 22% in the nine trading days after former chief executive Jensen Huang acknowledged an affair, CNBC reported. The Hill, citing The Wall Street Journal, reported a separate Securities and Exchange Commission probe into Nvidia, though its exact focus could not be confirmed. Nvidia’s board has said it will not reinstate Huang; Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO. Huang is scheduled to appear before congressional committees Dec. 1, followed by General Counsel Tim Teter on Dec. 2.
business.image_alt: California subpoenas Nvidia in investor-disclosure inquiry as shares slide

business.title: Amazon warns NYC shoppers delivery bill could add up to $5 per order
business.summary: Amazon began showing New York City shoppers notices warning that a proposed delivery law could add up to $5 per order. The Delivery Protection Act, also known as Intro 518, would require last-mile delivery companies to employ their workers directly rather than use independent delivery businesses such as those in Amazon
business.content: Amazon began showing New York City shoppers notices warning that a proposed delivery law could add up to $5 per order. The Delivery Protection Act, also known as Intro 518, would require last-mile delivery companies to employ their workers directly rather than use independent delivery businesses such as those in Amazon’s network. Amazon says the law could force it to move operations outside the city, slowing deliveries and raising costs. City Council Speaker Julie Menin called Amazon’s price warning misleading, while Mayor Zohran Mamdani supports the measure as a way to strengthen worker protections. Menin said she was open to changes, including dropping the ban on third-party delivery companies and instead licensing and regulating warehouse operations. The bill remains under council review; no vote is scheduled, though proponents are pressing for action before year-end.
business.image_alt: Amazon warns NYC shoppers delivery bill could add up to $5 per order

business.title: Japan inflation rises to 2.2%, strengthening December rate-hike bets
business.summary: Japan’s core consumer inflation rose to 2.2% year over year in October from 2.1% in September, remaining above the Bank of Japan’s 2% target for a second month and strengthening expectations of a December rate increase. The figure was below economists’ 2.3% forecast, while a gauge excluding fresh food and energy eased
business.content: Japan’s core consumer inflation rose to 2.2% year over year in October from 2.1% in September, remaining above the Bank of Japan’s 2% target for a second month and strengthening expectations of a December rate increase. The figure was below economists’ 2.3% forecast, while a gauge excluding fresh food and energy eased to 2.2% from 2.4%. Markets expect the central bank to raise its policy rate from 1.25% to 1.5% at its meeting ending Dec. 18. Higher energy costs contributed to the price increase as government support for household energy bills declined. Japan’s economy also contracted unexpectedly in the third quarter, and weak household consumption has complicated the case for tightening. The government is expected to restore energy subsidies in December; the Bank of Japan will weigh the inflation data at its next policy meeting.
business.image_alt: Japan inflation rises to 2.2%, strengthening December rate-hike bets

business.title: Vendor cyber incidents put customer data at risk at Chase, Visa, Mastercard
business.summary: JPMorgan Chase said Thursday that attackers accessed marketing data held by outside vendors that may include some customers’ names and email addresses. Mastercard separately said an incident at a third-party provider exposed a limited number of email addresses belonging to a small subset of cardholders in a benefits pr
business.content: JPMorgan Chase said Thursday that attackers accessed marketing data held by outside vendors that may include some customers’ names and email addresses. Mastercard separately said an incident at a third-party provider exposed a limited number of email addresses belonging to a small subset of cardholders in a benefits program. Visa said an incident involved an Asia-Pacific service provider but did not confirm that any customer data was exposed; it said its systems and payment data were unaffected. Reports later said thousands of Chase customer records had leaked online; the information reportedly did not include credit-card data or particularly sensitive personal data. Researchers who examined data posted by a group calling itself n0n found about 16,000 Chase customer email addresses, some phone numbers and account identifiers, and more than 100 employee email addresses. They said the records appeared connected to Chase’s Reserve card program but could not establish whether the material represented the complete dataset. The group’s claims of responsibility have not been independently verified. Mastercard confirmed a separate vendor incident involving a limited number of email addresses from a specific benefits program. Visa said an incident involved a service provider in Asia-Pacific and that its systems and payment data were unaffected; it did not confirm that customer data was exposed. Chase said it will contact affected customers and offer credit monitoring where appropriate. The companies have not identified the providers.
business.image_alt: Vendor cyber incidents put customer data at risk at Chase, Visa, Mastercard

business.title: Thanksgiving meal costs rise 6% as turkey prices climb
business.summary: The average cost of a traditional Thanksgiving dinner for 10 in the United States rose 6% from 2025 to $58.63, the first annual increase since 2022, the American Farm Bureau Federation said. A 16-pound frozen turkey averaged $23.68, up 10%, while milk, dinner rolls and cranberries also cost more. The Farm Bureau cited
business.content: The average cost of a traditional Thanksgiving dinner for 10 in the United States rose 6% from 2025 to $58.63, the first annual increase since 2022, the American Farm Bureau Federation said. A 16-pound frozen turkey averaged $23.68, up 10%, while milk, dinner rolls and cranberries also cost more. The Farm Bureau cited higher fuel and farm labor costs among the pressures on food production and transport. Rising demand for turkey and the industry's continued recovery from bird flu have also contributed to higher turkey prices. The 2026 meal cost remains below the 2022 record of $64.05. Regional costs ranged from $54.33 in the South to $61.57 in the Northeast.
business.image_alt: Thanksgiving meal costs rise 6% as turkey prices climb

science.title: COP31 draft backs disputed carbon capture targets, drops fossil-fuel language
science.summary: A revised draft at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, proposes a disputed expansion of carbon capture while dropping explicit language on transitioning away from fossil fuels. The draft proposes capturing at least 500 million tonnes of carbon dioxide annually by 2035 and working toward 1.3 billion to 2.5 bill
science.content: A revised draft at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, proposes a disputed expansion of carbon capture while dropping explicit language on transitioning away from fossil fuels. The draft proposes capturing at least 500 million tonnes of carbon dioxide annually by 2035 and working toward 1.3 billion to 2.5 billion tonnes; those figures remain bracketed for negotiation. Global energy-related carbon dioxide emissions are about 38 billion tonnes a year. Carbon capture is costly and has not been proven at the scale required to meet climate targets, the Financial Times reported. The proposal is part of a nine-page text issued by Australia and Turkey on Nov. 19. It also retains a 35% electrification goal but does not require the added electricity to be clean. Negotiators were expected to continue revising the draft before seeking unanimous approval. They also remained divided over the timing of upcoming climate-science assessments.
science.image_alt: COP31 draft backs disputed carbon capture targets, drops fossil-fuel language

science.title: Cincinnati Zoo hippo Fiona dies after swallowing visitor
science.summary: Fiona, a nine-year-old Nile hippopotamus at the Cincinnati Zoo, died on Nov. 19 after swallowing a visitor’s knit hat that accidentally landed in her enclosure about 11 days earlier. A ceiling fan deflected the hat through a gap above the viewing windows, the zoo said. Veterinarians provided round-the-clock care, inclu
science.content: Fiona, a nine-year-old Nile hippopotamus at the Cincinnati Zoo, died on Nov. 19 after swallowing a visitor’s knit hat that accidentally landed in her enclosure about 11 days earlier. A ceiling fan deflected the hat through a gap above the viewing windows, the zoo said. Veterinarians provided round-the-clock care, including fluids, medication and examinations, but specialists advised against surgery on the full-grown hippo. Experts said hippos’ size, difficulties with anesthesia and the challenge of locating an object in their long digestive tracts complicate treatment. Fiona drew a worldwide following after surviving a premature birth in 2017; she weighed 29 pounds, about half the usual birth weight for a Nile hippo, the zoo said.
science.image_alt: Cincinnati Zoo hippo Fiona dies after swallowing visitor

science.title: Record-strength El Niño set to peak in December, raising weather risks
science.summary: The World Meteorological Organization says the strengthening El Niño is expected to peak in December and is almost certain to persist through February 2027, with a chance of ranking among the strongest since 1950. The agency forecasts unusually warm conditions across much of the world and shifting rainfall patterns tha
science.content: The World Meteorological Organization says the strengthening El Niño is expected to peak in December and is almost certain to persist through February 2027, with a chance of ranking among the strongest since 1950. The agency forecasts unusually warm conditions across much of the world and shifting rainfall patterns that could increase drought and flood risks. U.S. seasonal outlooks favor above-average winter temperatures across much of the northern United States and wetter conditions with elevated coastal flooding risk in California. Unusually high tides beginning Nov. 24 could coincide with storms and heavy rain in California, though forecasters say storm timing and rainfall remain uncertain. High tides are also forecast for Dec. 23-25 and Jan. 21-22, extending the period when storm waves could push water inland.
science.image_alt: Record-strength El Niño set to peak in December, raising weather risks

science.title: COP31 talks expose dispute over timing of next climate science report
science.summary: Countries at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya launched the second five-yearly assessment of global progress under the Paris Agreement, while disputing whether the next major climate science reports will be ready to inform its conclusion in 2028. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the United Nation
science.content: Countries at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya launched the second five-yearly assessment of global progress under the Paris Agreement, while disputing whether the next major climate science reports will be ready to inform its conclusion in 2028. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the United Nations body that assesses climate research, has not agreed on a publication schedule. The European Union and groups representing small island and least-developed countries want the reports published in 2028; Saudi Arabia, India and China favor 2029, arguing that a faster timetable could limit participation by developing-country scientists. The IPCC’s October meeting ended without agreement, and another meeting is planned for December. A midweek letter from the COP31 presidency listed 21 unresolved negotiating issues.
science.image_alt: COP31 talks expose dispute over timing of next climate science report

science.title: African negotiators press for triple adaptation funding at COP31
science.summary: African negotiators at the U.N. climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, are seeking to triple annual adaptation finance to $120 billion by 2035, using an annual baseline of $40 billion they say developed countries committed to provide by 2025. The proposal was not accepted for formal negotiations, and the European Union say
science.content: African negotiators at the U.N. climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, are seeking to triple annual adaptation finance to $120 billion by 2035, using an annual baseline of $40 billion they say developed countries committed to provide by 2025. The proposal was not accepted for formal negotiations, and the European Union says the priority should be delivering existing pledges and making funds easier to access. Twenty-three African countries, including Uganda and Malawi, have yet to submit national adaptation plans that can help identify climate risks and support funding requests. The U.N. estimates developing countries will need $300 billion a year by 2035, but they received about 10% of that amount from developed countries in 2024. African civil society groups are also pressing for finance that does not add to debt and for measurable commitments on fossil fuel reductions. COP31 was scheduled to close on Friday, Nov. 20, with 21 issues unresolved.
science.image_alt: African negotiators press for triple adaptation funding at COP31

science.title: Brain study finds speech-planning region may aid communication devices
science.summary: A study published Nov. 19 in Science identifies a small region within Wernicke’s area that helps prepare words before people speak, challenging the view that the area mainly processes speech heard from others. The region, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus, became active before speech, and disrupting it caused
science.content: A study published Nov. 19 in Science identifies a small region within Wernicke’s area that helps prepare words before people speak, challenging the view that the area mainly processes speech heard from others. The region, the left posterior superior temporal gyrus, became active before speech, and disrupting it caused speech errors in stimulation and lesion tests. Researchers recorded brain activity in 28 people undergoing treatment for epilepsy or tumors. Stimulation tests involved 13 people, and an analysis of surgical cases also linked damage to the area with speech difficulties. In two people with paralysis, signals from the region helped researchers decode intended and heard speech, suggesting it could be explored as a target for communication devices for people with language disorders. Researchers presented the findings at the Society for Neuroscience meeting on Nov. 15.
science.image_alt: Brain study finds speech-planning region may aid communication devices

science.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo prepares to enter Mercury orbit after eight years
science.summary: The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission is due to enter orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21 after an eight-year journey of about 6 billion miles, becoming only the second mission to orbit the planet. Its two orbiters will investigate Mercury’s surface, interior and magnetic environment, including its unusually large meta
science.content: The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission is due to enter orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21 after an eight-year journey of about 6 billion miles, becoming only the second mission to orbit the planet. Its two orbiters will investigate Mercury’s surface, interior and magnetic environment, including its unusually large metal core, the origins of its magnetic field and ice in permanently shadowed craters. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival, and reaching Mercury requires careful braking against the Sun’s gravity. The European Mercury Planetary Orbiter will map the surface’s composition and study the interior; Japan’s orbiter will measure the magnetic field and the planet’s thin sodium exosphere. The spacecraft are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10, with science operations planned to begin in April 2027.
science.image_alt: European-Japanese BepiColombo prepares to enter Mercury orbit after eight years

science.title: COP31 draft recognizes carbon removal as delegates debate power target
science.summary: Negotiators at the United Nations COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, are considering draft language recognizing carbon dioxide removal’s role in meeting the long-term temperature goal, while debating a proposed global target to raise electricity’s share of final energy use from 23% to 35%. The draft also calls for
science.content: Negotiators at the United Nations COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, are considering draft language recognizing carbon dioxide removal’s role in meeting the long-term temperature goal, while debating a proposed global target to raise electricity’s share of final energy use from 23% to 35%. The draft also calls for expanding carbon capture and storage, which prevents new emissions rather than removing carbon dioxide already in the atmosphere. If adopted, it would be the first COP decision to explicitly refer to carbon dioxide removal, apart from a brief mention in 2023. The United Nations said earlier this year that crossing the Paris Agreement’s 1.5C warming threshold can no longer be prevented; returning below it by the end of the century would require deep emissions cuts alongside large-scale carbon removal. Critics say removal methods are unproven at the scale required, while the draft electricity target does not specify that power should come from clean sources. COP31 was scheduled to end Friday, Nov. 20, but difficult negotiations raised the prospect of an extension.
science.image_alt: COP31 draft recognizes carbon removal as delegates debate power target

sports.summary: After the first 10 matches of the 2026-27 Premier League season, ESPN predicted how all 20 clubs will finish, The Independent graded their starts, and The Athletic, part of The New York Times, surveyed supporters on whether they felt more or less optimistic than before the season. sports.content: The Colorado Rockies acquired right-handers Luis Castillo and Davis Martin from the Chicago White Sox on Thursday, sending left-hander Sean Sullivan and teenage catcher Douglas Veliz to Chicago. Colorado is taking on Castillo’s $22.75 million 2027 salary as part of the deal. Castillo posted an 8.42 ERA in 31 innings with Chicago, which sheds salary and opens innings for other pitchers in the trade. Martin recorded a 3.95 ERA over 146 innings in 2026. White Sox general manager Chris Getz said the club still needs pitching and will keep looking for ways to improve its staff.

sports.content: President Donald Trump announced Nov. 19 that he had posthumously pardoned Pete Rose, Major League Baseball’s career hits leader, who died in 2024 at 83. The pardon covers Rose’s 1990 federal tax convictions, not his ban from baseball for betting, and does not itself change his eligibility for the National Baseball Hall of Fame. Rose agreed to a permanent baseball ban in 1989 after an investigation found he bet on Cincinnati Reds games while playing for and managing the team from 1985 to 1987. In 2025, Major League Baseball Commissioner Rob Manfred restored Rose’s eligibility following his death, allowing him to be considered for the Hall of Fame. A committee could consider him in December 2027, with induction possible in 2028.

sports.content: Mercedes driver George Russell set the fastest time in the second practice session (FP2) for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, clocking 1:47.272 on a damp but drying track, 0.071 seconds ahead of Alpine’s Pierre Gasly. Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc was third. Heavy rain had prevented any timed laps in the opening session, and the track remained too slippery for slick tyres during FP2. Dry conditions are expected for qualifying and the race, and teams have one practice session left to gather dry-track data. The drivers’ and constructors’ titles are already decided, but 33 points separate second through sixth in the drivers’ standings with three races left. Qualifying is scheduled for Saturday, November 21, and the Grand Prix for Sunday, November 22.

sports.content: The Premier League has confirmed revised kick-off times and television coverage for its January 2027 fixtures, moving headline games including Manchester United-Liverpool and Manchester City-Arsenal into Sunday afternoon slots on Sky Sports. United host Liverpool at 4:30 p.m. on January 24, while City host Arsenal at the same time on January 31. Sky Sports and TNT Sports will share live coverage of several high-profile league matches. Other notable fixtures include Liverpool’s home Merseyside derby against Everton at 12:30 p.m. on January 30, live on TNT Sports, and Arsenal’s home match against Newcastle at 5:30 p.m. on January 23, live on Sky Sports. The league also said no two matchweeks over Christmas and New Year will be scheduled less than 60 hours apart. The 2027/28 season will begin on August 13, 2027, with its final round on May 21, 2028.

The team described the pe
sports.content: The Baltimore Ravens will deactivate cornerback Marlon Humphrey for Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers after he said on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Coach Jesse Minter announced Thursday that he had sent Humphrey home and that Humphrey would not practice. The team described the penalty as a one-game deactivation. Humphrey apologized Wednesday, saying he understood the effect of his words, and Minter said he was remorseful. Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott said an apology alone was insufficient, arguing the remark could hurt young Black residents who view the Ravens as role models. He invited Humphrey to meet with him and Baltimoreans who have returned to the community to help prevent others from repeating their mistakes. The Ravens play Carolina in Charlotte on Sunday, Nov. 22. Minter said the team’s internal conversations would remain private.

sports.title: NFL suspends Rams receiver Puka Nacua three games over conduct
sports.summary: The National Football League suspended Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua for three games without pay on Nov. 19 for violating its personal conduct policy. The suspension took effect immediately and overlaps with his time on injured reserve, where he must miss at least four games while recovering from knee ligam
sports.content: The National Football League suspended Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua for three games without pay on Nov. 19 for violating its personal conduct policy. The suspension took effect immediately and overlaps with his time on injured reserve, where he must miss at least four games while recovering from knee ligament sprains and turf toe. He is eligible for reinstatement Dec. 14 and could return when the Rams host the Dallas Cowboys on Dec. 20. The league did not publicly specify the policy violation. The suspension follows a civil lawsuit filed in March by a woman who alleges Nacua made an antisemitic remark and bit her during a New Year’s Eve outing. Nacua has denied the allegations through his attorney, who described the biting as “horseplay”. The league warned Nacua that further violations, including failure to meet diversion-program conditions, could bring more severe discipline, including banishment. Nacua has caught 70 passes for 715 yards and four touchdowns in seven games this season. The Rams are 6-4 after four straight wins, and fellow receiver Davante Adams is also on injured reserve. The Los Angeles Times reported that Nacua would not have access to the team facility before the Packers game but could access it during the final two weeks of his suspension.

sports.title: Premier League clubs back legal protection as Manchester City sponsors threaten lawsuits
sports.summary: Premier League clubs voted 18-2 in London on Nov. 19 to extend legal indemnity to five league board members if they face lawsuits from Manchester City sponsors airline Etihad Airways or telecommunications company Etisalat. The amendment covers chief executive Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittain and non-executive dir
sports.content: Premier League clubs voted 18-2 in London on Nov. 19 to extend legal indemnity to five league board members if they face lawsuits from Manchester City sponsors airline Etihad Airways or telecommunications company Etisalat. The amendment covers chief executive Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittain and non-executive directors Mai Fyfield, Dharmash Mistry and Matthew Ryder; all 20 clubs share the potential costs under the league’s collective-responsibility rules. The vote followed an independent commission’s September finding that City broke more than 100 financial rules between 2009 and 2018, including through “sham” sponsorship contracts that the commission said artificially inflated revenue by £830 million. City denies wrongdoing and is appealing, while Etihad and Etisalat have said they are considering legal action over the findings’ implications for them. The appeal and any sanction for City remain unresolved.
